body:
did you know: half the people who loved "blank space" missed the joke.

taylor built the whole song as satire -- a wink at the tabloid caricature of herself she'd finally decided was "kind of hilarious" once she stopped feeling attacked by it. the narrator is a cartoon on purpose: "a girl who's crazy but seductive but glamorous but nuts but manipulative." she's said only about half of listeners caught it was a joke; the rest took the man-eater at face value -- which was almost the point.

it worked commercially either way. after debuting at no. 18, "blank space" knocked her own "shake it off" out of the top spot in its third week -- making her the first woman in the hot 100's 56-year history to replace herself at no. 1 (only nine acts had ever done it, from the beatles to the black eyed peas). seven straight weeks at the top, eventually 8x platinum.

the best joke in pop is the one you can dance to before you get it.
